memory_candidates.content: When a record-amendment task narrows two acceptance-type names in one report's inventory sentence to one (e.g. 'Rabin or parity' -> 'Rabin alone'), check whether the same narrowing claim is restated independently in 2-3 other places in the SAME or a SIBLING report (an ingredient-table cell, a verdict paragraph's enumeration, an executive-summary bullet, a ROADMAP bullet). Each restatement is its own anchor with its own byte-identical-preservation obligations (an opening sentence, a closing sentence, an unrelated enumerated item like (O3)/(O4)) and must be independently re-measured with grep -cF immediately before editing, even when the semantic content of the edit is identical across all of them. Treating them as one edit risks either missing a restatement or over-editing a byte-identical-preservation zone.

git diff -U0's hunk count can under-count a Scope Hypothesis's predicted hunk count when two planned edits land in the same contiguous sentence run with no unchanged line between them -- they collapse into one diff hunk even though the plan's anchor table lists them as two separate dispositions. This is a diff-mechanics artifact, not a missed edit: verify against the anchor table's per-anchor grep -cF counts and required-substring checks, which are the authoritative verification criteria, rather than insisting the literal hunk count match the Scope Hypothesis's estimate.
